selected_result: Theorem 3.3: probabilistic componentwise backward error for matrix-vector multiplication

bibliographic_source.title: A New Approach to Probabilistic Rounding Error Analysis

task_clarification: For A in R^(m x n) and x in R^n, compute y=A*x in floating-point arithmetic under Model 2.1, obtaining yHat.
For every lambda>0, with probability at least Q(lambda,m*n), there exists DeltaA with yHat=(A+DeltaA)*x and |DeltaA|<=gammaTilde_n(lambda)*|A| componentwise.
Q and gammaTilde are exactly the Higham-Mary equations (3.1) and (2.1)-(2.2), conditional on independent, mean-zero operation errors bounded by u.
scope_constraints: Keep arbitrary rectangular m,n and the full vector output; one row alone is insufficient.
The source explains that inner-product and vector-operation loop orderings are covered; do not silently restrict to one ordering.
Do not assume the desired matrix perturbation or high-probability event in the execution model.
